deepdive.sec: Circular Materials / Waste Tire Recycling & Pyrolysis

bull_bear.body: Dividend of INR 3.5/share recommended. Funding mix for future capex: Internal accruals, unutilized DFI (Proparco) limits, and potential sale of unsold EPR credits. No immediate equity dilution planned despite expired QIP approval.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical volatility affecting energy/logistics costs; US trade policy shifts impacting indirect exports via SE Asia; Cheap Chinese virgin polymer imports undercutting recycled plastics; Delays in PCB approvals for EPR credit accrual on Pyrolysis units.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges FY26 as a 'transition year' with absorbed costs; emphasizes 'inflection point' for FY27; confident in long-term circular economy thesis and operational leverage from new assets.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management revealed that indirect exports to SE Asia (for tires sold to US) have not fully recovered despite direct US volume recovery; TPO pricing correlates with fuel oil but volume is constrained by bitumen shortage in road construction due to West Asia conflict; EPR credits for Pyrolysis (accruing retrospectively upon approval) could provide a significant one-time earnings boost in H1 FY27.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Reclaim Rubber: Export volumes -15%, Domestic +10%; margins pressured by 43% RM inflation in specific SKUs and lower-margin domestic mix. Pyrova Energy (Pyrolysis): Commissioned in H2; operating at >85% utilization; currently selling TPO to road/industrial fuel; rCB facility expected H2 FY27. Engineering Plastics: Automotive segment showing strong traction; Packaging segment pressured by cheap Chinese virgin PP imports. Polymer Composite: Discontinued due to weak viability/tariffs.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: FY26 margins compressed by raw material inflation (up to 43% in some SKUs), unfavorable product mix (shift to lower-margin domestic sales), and start-up costs of Pyrova. Pricing pass-through for RM inflation fully implemented from April 2026.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Expect restoration of export volumes in FY27; Domestic growth continuing. Margins: Reclaim Rubber margins to recover as export mix improves (exports are ~200-250bps higher margin); Pyrova Energy targeting high double-digit EBITDA margins upon full stabilization (FY28). Order Inflow: Stronger than FY26 average. Capex: INR 90-100cr planned for FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Order book described as 'much stronger and higher' than most of FY26 driven by new business wins and North American volume recovery; specific numeric value not disclosed.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Scaling Pyrova Energy to 45k tons pyrolysis capacity and 12k tons rCB by Feb 2027; moving TPO up the value chain from road surfacing to industrial furnaces and petchem feedstock; doubling new-tech Reclaim Rubber capacity to 700 tons/month; increasing circular material content in automotive OEMs.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: GRP Limited navigated a volatile FY26 marked by US tariff disruptions and raw material inflation, resulting in a 3% revenue decline and margin compression, but successfully commissioned its flagship Pyrova Energy platform which positions the company for high-double-digit margin expansion in FY27-FY28 as export volumes recover and rCB operations commence.

drhp.business: GRP is an integrated polymer/rubber recycling company operating across Reclaim Rubber, Engineering Plastics, Repurposed Polyolefins (via wholly owned subsidiary GRP Circular Solutions Limited), Polymer Composite & Custom Die-Forms, and Waste-to-Energy (branded Pyrova Energy) verticals. It serves over 400 customers globally, including 8 of the top 10 global tyre manufacturers, supplying materials used in tyre and automotive component manufacturing, ground transportation, agricultural and earth-moving equipment, packaging, and increasingly petrochemicals and infrastructure applications.

risks.note: Container shortages, rising freight costs, and geopolitical tensions could affect timely delivery and export margins; mitigated through geographic diversification and greater domestic-market focus.
Fluctuations in raw material prices and supply chain disruptions pose risks to cost management and production timelines, requiring proactive sourcing strategies and supplier diversification.
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and availability

risks.note: Although overall risk has reduced with greater regulatory clarity on pricing and a more stable EPR portal, implementation gaps in the policy framework, presence of non-compliant recyclers, external stakeholder dependencies, demand-supply imbalances, and delays with the plastics EPR portal continue to create operational uncertainty.
risks.risk: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) policy execution risk

risks.note: Despite a successful launch and major customer approvals, GRP Circular Solutions Limited (Repurposed Polyolefins) is currently operating below optimal capacity due to delays in scaling operations and supply chain bottlenecks.
Significant technology projects are underway (SAP system upgrades, DMS, shopfloor digitisation), but the pace of execution needs to accelerate to match the scale of the Company's growth ambitions.

The Company Secretary & Compliance Officer resigned effective 7th April 2026; the search for a replacement was under active progress as of the report date, leaving a KMP compliance role temporarily vacant.
